comparisons.title: Neutrophilic Dermatoses: Clinical–Histopathologic Comparison
comparisons.subtitle: Differentiate overlapping sterile neutrophilic reaction patterns

values.sweet: Abrupt tender erythematous–violaceous papules/plaques; pseudovesicular, pustular, bullous, or cellulitis-like variants.
values.pg: Painful pustule/nodule/bulla evolves into ulcer with violaceous undermined border; pathergy and cribriform scar.
values.nud: Evanescent erythematous macules/thin plaques, usually <24–48 h, often burning rather than pruritic.
values.rnd: Symmetric papules, plaques, nodules, annular lesions, or bullae in RA; often minimally symptomatic.
values.pngd: Umbilicated/crusted extensor papules, nodules, annular plaques, or rope-like cords.

values.sweet: Dense upper-dermal neutrophils with papillary dermal edema; leukocytoclasia may occur but primary vasculitis is absent.
values.pg: Nonspecific ulcer-edge neutrophilia/suppurative inflammation; secondary vasculitis may occur; biopsy mainly excludes mimics.
values.nud: Interstitial/perivascular neutrophils with leukocytoclasia, little edema, and no fibrinoid vessel-wall necrosis.
values.rnd: Dense dermal neutrophils, sometimes papillary microabscesses, without primary vasculitis.
values.pngd: Early neutrophils/LCV around altered collagen; mature palisaded granulomas and fibrosis. IGD is more interstitial and often nonvasculitic.

values.sweet: Myeloid malignancy, drugs/G-CSF, infection, IBD, autoimmune disease, pregnancy.
values.pg: IBD, inflammatory arthritis, hematologic malignancy, monoclonal gammopathy, postoperative/pathergy states.
values.nud: Schnitzler, CAPS, adult-onset Still disease, SLE and other systemic inflammatory disease.
values.rnd: Usually severe seropositive RA; occasionally other inflammatory disease.
values.pngd: RA most common; SLE, vasculitis, malignancy, infection, drugs.

values.pg: Progressive ulcer over days to months; healing is slow even after inflammation stops.
values.nud: Hours, usually no residual purpura or pigment.
values.pngd: Papules/plaques persist longer and evolve histologically with age.

values.sweet: Systemic glucocorticoid; local corticosteroid if limited.
values.pg: Wound care plus systemic glucocorticoid or ciclosporin for significant disease.
values.nud: Dapsone/colchicine and treatment of underlying disease.
values.rnd: Treat RA; topical/systemic corticosteroid, dapsone, colchicine, or hydroxychloroquine.
values.pngd: Treat underlying disease; topical/intralesional corticosteroid ± systemic anti-inflammatory therapy.

citations.quote: Review classifies neutrophilic dermatoses by clinical and histopathologic pattern and emphasizes exclusion of infection and systemic associations.
Review defines neutrophilic urticarial dermatosis as transient, usually nonpruritic lesions with dermal neutrophilia, leukocytoclasia, and no vasculitis.
A 65-patient series supports reactive granulomatous dermatitis as an umbrella for IGD, PNGD, and related patterns with frequent systemic associations.

comparisons.title: Painful Ulcer Mimics of Pyoderma Gangrenosum
comparisons.subtitle: Safety-critical distinctions before immunosuppression or debridement

values.pg: Rapid painful expansion; pain can be severe; may follow trauma.
values.nf: Hours to days; pain out of proportion, toxicity, anesthesia, crepitus, shock.
values.calc: Severe ischemic pain; retiform plaques/nodules evolve to necrosis, often in kidney disease.
values.vasc: Pain/burning with purpura, nodules, ulcers; systemic symptoms depend on vessel size.
values.lv: Recurrent painful retiform purpura and small punched-out ulcers around ankles.
values.venous: Chronic, often aching; improves with elevation/compression if arterial supply adequate.

values.pg: Violaceous, edematous, undermined inflammatory edge; pustules and pathergy.
values.nf: Poorly demarcated erythema, edema, bullae, ecchymosis, necrosis; no characteristic undermined border.
values.calc: Retiform purpura, firm subcutaneous plaques, black eschar; adipose sites often involved.
values.vasc: Palpable purpura (small vessel) or livedo/retiform purpura/nodules (medium vessel).
values.lv: Atrophie blanche, livedo racemosa, stellate scars near malleoli.
values.venous: Gaiter-area shallow irregular ulcer, edema, hemosiderin, lipodermatosclerosis.

values.pg: Deep active-edge biopsy; neutrophilia is supportive but nonspecific; culture separately.
values.nf: Operative exploration and deep tissue cultures are decisive; do not delay surgery for skin biopsy.
values.calc: Deep incisional biopsy only when benefit outweighs wound risk; calcified thrombosed arterioles and fat necrosis.
values.vasc: Fresh lesion for H&E; second specimen for DIF; biopsy deep enough for suspected medium vessels.
values.lv: Deep punch/incisional biopsy from edge; hyaline thrombosis with minimal primary vessel-wall inflammation.
values.venous: Usually clinical/vascular testing; biopsy atypical/nonhealing edge to exclude malignancy or inflammatory ulcer.

values.pg: Repeated debridement can worsen pathergy; still exclude/treat true infection.
values.nf: Delay in surgical source control is lethal.
values.calc: Immunosuppression without recognizing occlusive calcific disease can worsen risk.
values.vasc: Treating morphology without checking kidney, lung, GI, neurologic, or systemic involvement.
values.lv: Mislabeling as vasculitis and overlooking thrombosis/compression/vascular factors.
values.venous: Immunosuppression instead of compression and venous management.

citations.quote: International Delphi criteria for ulcerative pyoderma gangrenosum combine an ulcer-edge neutrophilic biopsy with validated clinical minor criteria.
Algorithmic review emphasizes morphology, vessel depth, appropriately timed biopsy, and systemic evaluation in cutaneous vasculitis.
Livedoid vasculopathy is an occlusive microvascular disorder distinguished from inflammatory vasculitis by clinical and histopathologic synthesis.
